official_measurement_examples.name: SPA classification scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's June 2026 SPA dataset contains classified sites and states that proposed sites are not included.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ramsar listing scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's July 2026 Ramsar dataset contains listed sites and states that proposed sites are not included.

official_measurement_examples.name: SAC boundary update context
official_measurement_examples.fact: JNCC's April 2026 SAC dataset notes March 2026 network updates can reflect designation, boundary amendments, corrections or base-map changes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Likely significant effect trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance requires appropriate assessment where a likely significant effect cannot be excluded on objective information, including in-combination effects.

official_measurement_examples.name: Screening and mitigation separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Habitats guidance preserves the distinction between screening for likely significant effects and the later appropriate-assessment stage where mitigation can be considered.

official_measurement_examples.name: Integrity test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Appropriate assessment must provide sufficiently precise findings for the competent authority to rule out adverse effects on site integrity in view of conservation objectives.

official_measurement_examples.name: Functionally linked effects
official_measurement_examples.fact: Habitats assessment can need to consider effects outside the mapped site boundary where they are liable to affect designated features or conservation objectives.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: SAC, SPA or Ramsar mapping, HRA screening, appropriate assessment, derogation and planning permission are separate evidential and legal stages and none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: SAC SPA or Ramsar geometry is designation evidence not a complete planning decision
an intersection with a habitats site is not automatic planning refusal
absence from one dataset is not proof no habitats-site effect exists
proposed candidate and designated site status must not be merged
screening for likely significant effects is distinct from appropriate assessment
mitigation evidence must not be silently applied at the wrong HRA stage
appropriate assessment is not planning permission
planning permission is not a completed habitats integrity test
functionally linked habitat effects can occur outside mapped designation boundaries
derogation is an exceptional legal route not a routine mitigation score
site conservation objectives must be retained with the affected feature and date
historic boundary versions must not override newer authoritative revisions silently
habitats-site compliance does not determine ownership access or infrastructure capacity
no parcel habitats clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Natural England, JNCC, Planning Data, data.gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk sources were checked on 2026-07-26. June-July 2026 SPA/Ramsar and March 2026 SAC network data were preserved as designation and assessment evidence, not parcel clearance.
